label: copy phase (every step after <DEL>)
explanation: Fires on every copy-phase step (t > L, i.e. the steps where the model outputs original tokens 1..L-1 with its own outputs fed back), and essentially never in the original phase or on the <DEL> step itself (110 + 4 stray activations out of 2.7M). Token-independent: rate and mass are flat across input token, output token, first token, digit count. Magnitude peaks at the first copy step (recall_idx 1, right after <DEL>, ~1.0 of max), decays over the next 2-3 steps to ~0.65-0.7 and then plateaus or rises slightly; sequences with longer L reach higher peaks. Does not fire on the delimiter step or any original-phase input.

issues: On test, phase == 2 scores precision 1.0, recall 0.99995, F1 0.99998, mass recall 0.999998 and correlation 0.987, so the reported scores are confirmed.

Test misses (127 steps, 0.0% of activation mass) all appear to be the last original token (step 8, orig_idx 8) of L=9 sequences, with tiny activations of 0.03-0.04 of max. This is a weak spill-over just before <DEL>, not a meaningful counterexample class. Inside phase 2 there are no false positives.

On dev the feature is active on 100% of steps at every recall_idx (1-8), with no in_tok dependence. The magnitude decay seen in the miss renderings (about 0.93-0.96 at recall_idx 1, falling to about 0.65-0.75) matches the explanation. As the explanation admits, the decay is qualitative and was not measured systematically.
Minor wording issue: the explanation's 't > L' describes the copy-phase steps correctly (recall_idx >= 1). The <DEL> step at t = L is correctly excluded (4 activations on dev).
